topics.name: Cain's line and the birth of Seth
topics.description: Cain builds a city and his descendants include tent-dwellers, musicians and metalworkers, while Lamech boasts of killing a man. Adam and Eve have Seth in place of Abel, and in Seth's day men begin to call on the name of the LORD.
evidence: Name some of Cain's descendants and what they were known for (4:20-22)
Contrast Lamech's words in 4:23-24 with the birth of Seth and the calling on the LORD's name in 4:25-26
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Genesis 4 ends with two family lines, Cain's and Seth's, and what is said about Seth's son Enos?

topics.name: From Adam to Noah: the first genealogy
topics.description: Genesis 5 lists ten generations from Adam to Noah, repeating that each one lived a number of years and died, except Enoch, who walked with God and was not, for God took him. Lamech names his son Noah with a hope of comfort from the cursed ground.
evidence: Point out the repeated phrase 'and he died' in the chapter and the one exception in verse 24
Explain what Lamech hoped for when he named Noah (5:29)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Genesis 5 tells us about Enoch, and why the chapter keeps repeating that each man died?

topics.name: The sons of God and the daughters of men
topics.description: As men multiply, the sons of God take wives of the daughters of men, and the LORD limits man's days to one hundred and twenty years. The text notes mighty men of renown born in those days.
evidence: Summarise what Genesis 6:1-4 reports happening and what the LORD says in 6:3
Say honestly which points in the passage are plainly stated and which are debated
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell what Genesis 6:1-4 says, and explain why the identity of the 'sons of God' needs careful study of the text?

topics.name: A new start: blessing, food and the sanctity of life
topics.description: After the flood God blesses Noah and his sons, tells them to be fruitful, puts the animals under their hand, permits meat but not blood, and requires an account for the shedding of man's blood because man is made in God's image.
evidence: List what God tells Noah's family to do and what He permits and forbids in 9:1-5
Explain the reason given in 9:6 for the penalty for shedding man's blood
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why God says in Genesis 9:6 that shedding man's blood is so serious?

topics.name: Noah's vineyard and the curse on Canaan
topics.description: Noah plants a vineyard, becomes drunk and lies uncovered in his tent. Ham tells his brothers, while Shem and Japheth cover their father, and Noah then curses Canaan and blesses the LORD God of Shem.
evidence: Contrast what Ham did with what Shem and Japheth did (9:22-23)
State exactly whom Noah curses and whom he blesses (9:25-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened in Noah's tent and how Shem, Ham and Japheth each responded?

topics.name: The table of nations
topics.description: Genesis 10 traces the families of Japheth, Ham and Shem after the flood, naming nations, lands and tongues, including Nimrod's kingdom beginning at Babel. It closes by saying the nations were divided in the earth after the flood.
evidence: Name Noah's three sons and one nation or person listed under each
Find where Nimrod and Babel appear in the chapter (10:8-10)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Genesis 10 teaches about where the nations came from?

topics.name: From Shem to Abram's family
topics.description: A second genealogy runs from Shem to Terah and his sons Abram, Nahor and Haran. It notes that Haran died in Ur, that Sarai was barren, and that Terah set out for Canaan but settled in Haran, where he died.
evidence: Trace the line from Shem to Abram in 11:10-26
Say what is told about Sarai in 11:30 and where Terah's journey stopped (11:31-32)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Genesis 11:10-32 introduces Abram and Sarai, and why Sarai's barrenness matters?

topics.name: Abram in Egypt
topics.description: A famine sends Abram down to Egypt, where he asks Sarai to say she is his sister for fear of being killed. Pharaoh takes her, the LORD plagues his house, and Pharaoh sends Abram away with his wife and all he had.
evidence: Explain why Abram told Sarai to say she was his sister (12:11-13)
Say who acts to rescue Sarai (12:17)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell what happened in Egypt and say who protected Sarai?

topics.name: Abram and Lot separate
topics.description: Abram returns to Bethel and calls on the LORD. Strife between the herdmen leads Abram to offer Lot his choice of land; Lot chooses the plain near Sodom, and the LORD then renews the promise of land and seed to Abram.
evidence: Describe how Abram settled the quarrel and what Lot chose
Say what the LORD promises Abram after Lot leaves (13:14-17)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Abram handled the quarrel with Lot, and what God promised him afterward?

topics.name: Abram rescues Lot
topics.description: Four kings defeat the kings of the plain and carry off Lot with his goods. Abram arms 318 trained servants, pursues them by night and brings back Lot, the goods and the people.
evidence: Explain why Abram went to war (14:12-14)
Describe how he pursued and what he brought back (14:14-16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why Abram went after the four kings and what he recovered?

topics.name: Melchizedek blesses Abram
topics.description: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, brings bread and wine and blesses Abram, who gives him tithes of all. Abram refuses the king of Sodom's goods, saying he has lifted his hand to the LORD, the most high God.
evidence: Say who Melchizedek is according to 14:18 and what he does and says
Explain why Abram refuses to take anything from the king of Sodom (14:22-23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what Melchizedek did for Abram and what Abram gave him?

topics.name: Hagar and the birth of Ishmael
topics.description: Sarai, still childless, gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram; Hagar conceives and is treated harshly and flees. The angel of the LORD finds her at a spring, tells her to return, promises many descendants and names her son Ishmael, and she calls God the one who sees her.
evidence: Explain how Hagar came to be Abram's wife (16:1-3)
Tell what the angel of the LORD says to Hagar and what she calls the LORD (16:7-13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened to Hagar in the wilderness and what she learned about God?

topics.name: The LORD visits Abraham and Sarah
topics.description: The LORD appears to Abraham in the plains of Mamre as three men; Abraham hurries to feed them. One says Sarah will have a son at the appointed time, Sarah laughs inside the tent, and the LORD asks whether anything is too hard for Him.
evidence: Describe Abraham's hospitality to the three men (18:2-8)
Repeat the question the LORD asks in 18:14 and say what it is about
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what the visitors promised Sarah and why she laughed?

topics.name: Abraham pleads for Sodom
topics.description: The LORD tells Abraham He will see whether the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is as great as it seems. Abraham draws near and asks whether the Judge of all the earth will do right, and the LORD agrees to spare the city for fifty, then down to ten righteous.
evidence: Say why the LORD decides to tell Abraham what He will do (18:17-19)
Trace the numbers Abraham names and the LORD's answers (18:24-32)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Abraham asked the LORD about Sodom and how the LORD answered?

topics.name: Sodom and Gomorrah are destroyed
topics.description: Two angels come to Lot in Sodom, the men of the city press against his house, and the angels strike them with blindness. They lead Lot, his wife and daughters out; the LORD rains brimstone and fire on the cities and Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.
evidence: Describe how the angels protected Lot and urged him to leave (19:10-17)
Say what God did to the cities and why 19:29 says He remembered Abraham
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell how Lot was brought out of Sodom and what happened to the cities?

topics.name: Lot's daughters and the birth of Moab and Ammon
topics.description: Lot goes up out of Zoar to live in a cave with his two daughters. Fearing no man remains to give them children, they make their father drunk and conceive sons, Moab and Ben-ammi, who become the fathers of the Moabites and Ammonites.
evidence: State the origin of the Moabites and Ammonites as given in 19:37-38
Observe how the text reports the daughters' plan without commending it
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say which nations descend from Lot's daughters according to Genesis 19:30-38?

topics.name: Abimelech takes Sarah
topics.description: In Gerar, Abraham again calls Sarah his sister and King Abimelech takes her. God warns Abimelech in a dream that he is a dead man, withheld him from sin, and tells him to restore her, for Abraham is a prophet who will pray for him.
evidence: Explain how God intervened to keep Abimelech from touching Sarah (20:3-6)
Say what Abraham does for Abimelech at the end of the chapter (20:17-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how God protected Sarah in Gerar and what Abraham's reason was for saying she was his sister?

topics.name: Hagar and Ishmael are sent away
topics.description: After Isaac is weaned, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and asks that he and Hagar be cast out. God tells Abraham that his seed will be called in Isaac but he will also make a nation of Ishmael; in the wilderness God hears the boy's voice and opens Hagar's eyes to a well.
evidence: Say what God told Abraham in 21:12-13
Describe how God provided for Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness (21:17-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what God promised about Ishmael, even as Isaac was the child of promise?

topics.name: Abraham and Abimelech at Beersheba
topics.description: Abimelech and Phichol ask Abraham to swear he will not deal falsely with them. Abraham reproves Abimelech about a seized well, the two make a covenant with seven ewe lambs as a witness, and Abraham calls on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.
evidence: Explain why Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs (21:28-30)
Say how Beersheba got its name (21:31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the well at Beersheba led to a covenant between Abraham and Abimelech?

topics.name: Abraham buries Sarah at Machpelah
topics.description: Sarah dies in Hebron, and Abraham, calling himself a stranger and sojourner, negotiates with the sons of Heth to buy the cave of Machpelah from Ephron for four hundred shekels of silver. He buries Sarah there.
evidence: Describe how Abraham obtained the burial place and what he paid (23:8-16)
Explain why a purchase of land in Canaan is notable in view of God's promise (cf. 13:15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Abraham came to own a piece of the promised land?

topics.name: A wife for Isaac
topics.description: Abraham sends his eldest servant under oath to his own kindred to find a wife for Isaac, not from the Canaanites. At the well the servant prays, Rebekah, a granddaughter of Abraham's brother Nahor, answers the sign, and after her family agrees she goes with him and marries Isaac.
evidence: Retell the servant's prayer at the well and how Rebekah answered it (24:12-20)
Point to places where the servant and Laban and Bethuel credit the LORD (24:27, 24:50)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Abraham's servant found Rebekah and who he said had guided him?

topics.name: Abraham's death and Ishmael's line
topics.description: Abraham takes Keturah, gives all he has to Isaac and gifts to his other sons, and dies at one hundred and seventy-five. Isaac and Ishmael bury him at Machpelah, God blesses Isaac, and the generations of Ishmael's twelve princes are listed.
evidence: Say who inherited Abraham's possessions and who buried him (25:5, 25:9)
Count the sons of Ishmael called princes (25:13-16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened after Abraham died and how God treated Isaac?

topics.name: Isaac in Gerar
topics.description: In a famine the LORD tells Isaac not to go to Egypt and repeats the promise made to Abraham. Isaac calls Rebekah his sister, is rebuked by Abimelech, prospers, digs wells that herdsmen contest, and the LORD appears at Beersheba before Abimelech makes a covenant with him.
evidence: Compare Isaac's words about Rebekah with Abraham's in chapters 12 and 20
Name the three wells Isaac dug after Gerar and what each name recalls (26:20-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how God renewed His promise to Isaac and what happened with the wells?

topics.name: Jacob sent to Padan-aram
topics.description: Isaac blesses Jacob, charges him not to marry a Canaanite and sends him to Laban's house for a wife, with the blessing of Abraham. Esau, seeing this, marries a daughter of Ishmael.
evidence: State what Isaac charges Jacob and the blessing he pronounces (28:1-4)
Say what Esau does in response (28:6-9)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jacob was sent away to Laban and what Isaac asked God to give him?

topics.name: Jacob, Rachel and Leah
topics.description: At a well Jacob meets Rachel and serves Laban seven years for her, but Laban gives him Leah first and Jacob serves seven more for Rachel. The LORD sees that Leah is hated and opens her womb, and she bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah.
evidence: Describe the deception on the wedding night and how Laban explained it (29:23-27)
Name Leah's four sons and note which one is Judah (29:32-35)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob came to marry both Leah and Rachel and what the LORD did for Leah?

topics.name: Jacob's sons are born and his flocks increase
topics.description: Rachel and Leah compete, giving their maids to Jacob, and sons are born including Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun and Dinah. God remembers Rachel and she bears Joseph; Jacob then bargains with Laban over the flocks and grows exceedingly rich.
evidence: Match each son with his mother as the chapter reports (Bilhah, Zilpah, Leah, Rachel)
Describe the wages Jacob proposed to Laban and the result (30:31-43)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how the family of Jacob grew in Haran and which son was born to Rachel?

topics.name: Jacob flees from Laban
topics.description: After Laban's sons complain and Laban's face turns against him, the LORD tells Jacob to return to his kindred. Jacob leaves in secret, Rachel takes her father's household images, and Laban pursues him but is warned by God in a dream not to speak good or bad; the two make a covenant with a heap of stones.
evidence: Say what God told Jacob in 31:3 and 31:13
Explain how God protected Jacob when Laban caught up with him (31:24, 31:42)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jacob left Laban secretly and how God kept him safe?

topics.name: Jacob prepares to meet Esau
topics.description: Angels of God meet Jacob at Mahanaim. Hearing that Esau is coming with four hundred men, Jacob divides his company, prays to the God of Abraham and Isaac, reminding Him of His promise, and sends droves of animals ahead as a present.
evidence: Summarise Jacob's prayer in 32:9-12 and note what promises he recalls
Describe the present he sent to Esau and why (32:13-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob responded when he heard Esau was coming with four hundred men?

topics.name: Jacob and Esau meet
topics.description: Jacob bows seven times as Esau runs to embrace him, and the two weep. Jacob urges Esau to accept the present, they part, and Jacob settles near Shechem, buys a field and raises an altar.
evidence: Describe how Esau greeted Jacob in 33:4
Say what Jacob did when he arrived near Shechem (33:18-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Jacob and Esau finally met after so many years?

topics.name: Dinah and the men of Shechem
topics.description: Shechem takes Dinah and defiles her, then asks to marry her. Jacob's sons answer deceitfully and demand circumcision; on the third day Simeon and Levi kill the males of the city, and Jacob rebukes them for troubling him.
evidence: Explain how the sons of Jacob used circumcision to deceive the men of Shechem (34:13-25)
Note Jacob's reaction in 34:30 and what the text reports of Simeon and Levi's reply
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Simeon and Levi did at Shechem and how their father responded?

topics.name: Back to Bethel: God confirms Israel's name
topics.description: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel; Jacob has his household put away their strange gods. At Bethel God blesses him, repeats that his name is Israel, and renews the promise of nations and land; Rachel dies bearing Benjamin, and Isaac dies at one hundred and eighty.
evidence: Say what Jacob told his household to do before going to Bethel (35:2-4)
List the twelve sons of Jacob by their mothers (35:22-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what God said to Jacob at Bethel in Genesis 35 and who the twelve sons of Jacob were?

topics.name: The generations of Esau, who is Edom
topics.description: Genesis 36 lists Esau's wives, sons and chiefs, notes that he moved to Mount Seir because the land could not bear both his and Jacob's herds, and lists the Horite families and the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over Israel.
evidence: Find the verse that says Esau is Edom and the verse that says why he moved (36:1, 36:6-8)
Point out the phrase about kings reigning before any king ruled Israel (36:31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain who the Edomites came from according to Genesis 36?

topics.name: Judah and Tamar
topics.description: Judah's sons Er and Onan die, and he withholds his third son Shelah from Tamar. Tamar disguises herself, conceives by Judah, produces his signet, cord and staff, and Judah says she is more righteous than he; she bears twins.
evidence: Say what Tamar did and what proof she showed Judah (38:14-25)
Quote or state Judah's verdict in 38:26 and say why he gives it
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Judah says Tamar was more righteous than he was?

topics.name: Joseph in Potiphar's house
topics.description: Joseph is bought by Potiphar in Egypt, and the LORD is with him so that all prospers in his hand. When Potiphar's wife presses him he refuses as a great wickedness before God; she falsely accuses him and he is put in prison, where the LORD is still with him.
evidence: Give Joseph's reason for refusing Potiphar's wife (39:8-9)
Note how often the chapter says the LORD was with Joseph (39:2, 39:21, 39:23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Joseph did when Potiphar's wife tempted him and what happened to him afterward?

topics.name: The butler and the baker's dreams
topics.description: In prison Joseph serves Pharaoh's chief butler and chief baker, who each dream. Saying that interpretations belong to God, Joseph tells the butler he will be restored and the baker hanged; it happens in three days, but the butler forgets Joseph.
evidence: Compare the two dreams and Joseph's interpretations (40:9-19)
Say what Joseph asks of the butler and what happens (40:14, 40:23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Joseph interpreted the two prisoners' dreams and who he said gives interpretations?

topics.name: Joseph's brothers come to Egypt
topics.description: In the famine Jacob sends ten sons to buy grain in Egypt while keeping Benjamin at home. Joseph recognises them and remembers his dreams, accuses them of spying, binds Simeon and sends the rest home with the demand to bring Benjamin; their money is found in their sacks.
evidence: Point to 42:6-9 and say why the brothers do not know Joseph but he knows them
Say what the brothers admit to one another in 42:21-22
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Joseph demanded of his brothers and why they said they were guilty?

topics.name: The second journey with Benjamin
topics.description: With the grain eaten, Judah promises to be surety for Benjamin, and Jacob reluctantly lets him go with a gift and double money. Joseph has the brothers brought to his house for a meal, weeps in his chamber on seeing Benjamin, and serves Benjamin five times as much.
evidence: Say what Judah offers his father in 43:8-9
Describe Joseph's reaction on seeing Benjamin (43:29-31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob was persuaded to send Benjamin and what Joseph did when he saw him?

topics.name: The silver cup and Judah's plea
topics.description: Joseph has his silver cup put in Benjamin's sack and sends his steward after the brothers. When the cup is found Judah pleads with Joseph, tells how Jacob loves the boy, and offers himself as a bondman in Benjamin's place.
evidence: Explain how the cup came to be in Benjamin's sack (44:1-2, 44:12)
Summarise Judah's offer and the reason he gives (44:32-34)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Judah offered to do for Benjamin and why?

topics.name: Joseph makes himself known
topics.description: Joseph cannot hold back and tells his brothers he is Joseph, saying not to be grieved that they sold him, for God sent him before them to preserve life. Pharaoh invites the family to Egypt, and Jacob's spirit revives when he hears Joseph is alive.
evidence: Retell what Joseph says in 45:4-8 about who sent him to Egypt
Say how Jacob reacted to the news (45:26-28)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Joseph understood what had happened to him and what he told his brothers?

topics.name: Jacob goes down to Egypt
topics.description: At Beersheba God tells Israel not to fear going down into Egypt, promising to make him a great nation there, go down with him and bring him up again. The household that came into Egypt is listed, and Joseph meets his father in Goshen and prepares them to speak to Pharaoh as shepherds.
evidence: State God's three promises to Jacob in 46:3-4
Give the total number of Jacob's house who came into Egypt (46:26-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Jacob before he went down to Egypt?

topics.name: Jacob before Pharaoh
topics.description: Joseph presents his brothers and father to Pharaoh, who gives them the land of Goshen to dwell in. Jacob blesses Pharaoh and describes his years as a pilgrimage, few and evil.
evidence: Say what land Pharaoh gave Jacob's family and what their trade was (47:3-6)
Report what Jacob says about the years of his pilgrimage (47:9)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell where Jacob's family settled in Egypt and who blessed whom in Pharaoh's court?

topics.name: The famine and Pharaoh's ownership of the land
topics.description: As the famine deepens Joseph gathers the money of Egypt and Canaan, then takes the people's cattle and finally their land in exchange for bread. The people become Pharaoh's servants and give a fifth of the increase, while the priests' land is not bought.
evidence: List in order what the people gave Joseph for bread (47:14-20)
State the law Joseph made about the fifth part (47:26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Joseph handled the famine in Egypt and what the people said in return (47:25)?

topics.name: Israel's oath and the blessing of Ephraim and Manasseh
topics.description: Israel makes Joseph swear to bury him with his fathers, then recalls God Almighty's promise at Luz and takes Ephraim and Manasseh as his own. He crosses his hands to bless the younger Ephraim first, over Joseph's objection, and says God will bring them back to the land of their fathers.
evidence: Say where Jacob asked to be buried and who swore to do it (47:29-31)
Explain what was unusual about the way Jacob blessed the two boys (48:13-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob blessed Joseph's sons and what he said God would do for the family?

topics.name: Jacob blesses his twelve sons
topics.description: Jacob gathers his sons to tell what will befall them in the last days, speaking in turn to Reuben, Simeon and Levi, Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Joseph and Benjamin. The chapter names these the twelve tribes of Israel; Judah's blessing is treated separately.
evidence: Say what Jacob says about Reuben and why (49:3-4)
Find the verse that calls the twelve sons the tribes of Israel (49:28)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name at least six of Jacob's sons and say one thing Jacob said about one of them?

topics.name: The death and burial of Jacob
topics.description: Jacob charges his sons to bury him in the cave of Machpelah with Abraham, Isaac and their wives, and then dies. Joseph has him embalmed, Egypt mourns, and a great company goes up to Canaan to bury him there.
evidence: Say who is already buried in the cave according to 49:31
Describe who went up with Joseph to bury Jacob (50:7-9)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell where Jacob was buried and why it was the same place as Abraham and Sarah?

Genesis 9:18 continues the account of Noah's sons after the blessing of 9:1-7
Genesis 10:1 lists the generations of the three sons named in 9:18-19
Genesis 11:10 resumes the line of Shem listed in 10:21-31
Abram has gone to Canaan at the LORD's call in 12:1-9 before the famine of 12:10
Genesis 13:1 begins with Abram going up out of Egypt with Lot
Lot is captured in 14:12 because he settled near Sodom in 13:11-12
Melchizedek meets Abram on his return from the slaughter of the kings (14:17)

The men rise up toward Sodom in 18:16 after the announcement to Sarah

Genesis 20:1 says Abraham journeyed from there after the events at Mamre and Sodom
Genesis 21:8 begins when Isaac, born in 21:1-7, is weaned
Hagar and Ishmael are introduced in chapter 16
Genesis 21:22 involves Abimelech, whom Abraham met in chapter 20
Genesis 23 follows the offering of Isaac and the news of Nahor's family in 22:20-24
Genesis 24:67 says Isaac was comforted after his mother's death recorded in chapter 23
Genesis 25:1 follows Isaac's marriage in chapter 24
Genesis 26 continues Isaac's story after the birth of Jacob and Esau in 25:24-26
Genesis 28:1-9 follows Jacob's blessing in 27 and Esau's marriages noted in 26:34-35
Jacob reaches the east country in 29:1 after the vision at Bethel in 28:10-22
The sons of chapter 30 are born in the rivalry begun in chapter 29
Genesis 31:1 follows the growth of Jacob's flocks and household in chapter 30
Jacob goes on his way in 32:1 after parting from Laban in 31:55
Genesis 33:1 shows Esau arriving with the four hundred men reported in 32:6
Genesis 33 follows Jacob's night at Peniel, 32:22-32
The events of chapter 34 happen at Shechem, where Jacob settled in 33:18
God tells Jacob to go to Bethel in 35:1 after the events at Shechem
Genesis 35:1-7 refers to the altar at Bethel where God appeared when Jacob fled from Esau
Genesis 36 follows the burial of Isaac by Esau and Jacob in 35:29
Genesis 38:1 begins at the time Judah left his brothers, after Joseph was sold in chapter 37
Judah is Leah's son born in 29:35
Genesis 39:1 says Joseph was brought down to Egypt, where he was sold in 37:36
Pharaoh's officers are put in the prison where Joseph was bound (40:3), as told in 39:20
Joseph is governor of Egypt in 42:6 after his rise in chapter 41
The journey in chapter 43 is the one Joseph demanded in 42:20
Genesis 44:1 follows the meal at Joseph's house in 43:34
Joseph cannot refrain himself in 45:1 after Judah's plea in 44:18-34
Israel journeys in 46:1 in response to the news and invitation of 45:9-28
Joseph tells Pharaoh in 47:1 of the arrival announced in 46:31-34
Genesis 47:13 returns to the famine after the settlement of Jacob's family
Genesis 47:27 continues from the famine account with Israel dwelling in Goshen
Jacob calls all his sons in 49:1 after blessing Joseph's sons in chapter 48
Genesis 49:29-33 is Jacob's charge to his sons that ends his blessing of them
The cave of Machpelah named in 49:30 is the field Abraham bought in chapter 23
